newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr firms vs yen in Tokyo, eyes on output data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr firms vs yen in Tokyo, eyes on output data.

text.p: The dollar firmed against the yen on short-covering by midday Tokyo on Friday, with the market largely focusing on the release of Japan's preliminary industrial output data due out at 0430 GMT, dealers said.
As uncertainty remains over the data, most market participants were eager to square their dollar short positions, which kept the dollar's downside solid, they added.
"Traders want to square their positions amid uncertainty over the industrial output data," a city bank dealer said.
A trust bank dealer said the fact that the recent release of Japan's quarterly "tankan" exceeded the market forecasts reminded them to keep a cautious stance ahead of the release of the output data.
Economists polled this week by Reuters forecast increases ranging from 1.2 percent to 3.0 percent in May output, compared with a revised month-on-month drop of 0.5 percent in April.
The Trade Ministry expects major manufacturers' output to show a 2.7 percent rise in May.

Speculative buying emerged around midday due to talk that tensions may be emerging on the Korean peninsula boosted the greenback as a safe-haven currency. The thin trade exaggerated such moves, pushing up the dollar towards 114 yen.
Previously, stop-loss sales were triggered near 113.40-50 yen, pushing the dollar higher to break the initial resistance point of early trading at 113.40 yen, dealers said.
But some exporter sales were detected on rises, a long-term credit bank dealer said.
The market now focusing on a speech by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita, which started at 0340 GMT.
Earlier in the day, the dollar was well-supported at 113 yen with bids from importers and Japanese investors. Meanwhile, some trust banks were said to be interested in selling dollars on the topside.

Some dealers said stronger-than-expected industrial output data could pave the way for the dollar to fall below 113 yen, while others said speculation of a strong result was already factored into the market.
Market participants have been focusing on the data for clues on Japanese interest rates in wake of unexpectedly strong figures in BOJ's tankan report on Wednesday.
In early afternoon, BOJ's Matsushita said there are signs that gradual economic recovery is continuing.
He added that Japan's economic recovery is highly likely to overcome the temporary setback and that Japan's policy is aimed at strengthening recovery.
The dollar closed at 113.10/20 yen and 1.7250/60 marks in New York on Thursday.
